title: Dina Nath Saw v. State of U.P. and Others
court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
coram: Satya Poot Mehrotra, J.; Bharati Sapru, J. (31.5.2011); Manoj Kumar Gupta, J.; Prashant Kumar, J. (9.5.2023)
disposition: Writ dismissed for want of prosecution.
headnote: Challenging a 9 May 2011 citation for deposit of a theft-of-electricity assessment, the petitioner alleged that no provisional assessment was served and the Electricity Act, 2003 and U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005 were not followed. The 2011 Division Bench issued notice and stayed recovery till the next date on a without-prejudice deposit of Rs. 71,000 after the licensee could not state the mode of sending the assessments. In 2023 none appeared to press even in revised call; the writ was dismissed for want of prosecution.
facts: Dina Nath Saw was prosecuted for alleged theft of electricity and granted bail. He claimed that no provisional assessment was served and he had no chance to object, yet a Citation dated 9 May 2011 demanded deposit of the theft assessment without complying with the Electricity Act, 2003 and the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005. The licensee said both assessments were sent and the Code was followed, but could not state the mode of service.

holding_units.topic: dismissal for want of prosecution; theft-assessment citation
holding_units.holding: The 2011 Division Bench issued notice and stayed recovery under the 9 May 2011 citation till the next date, conditional on deposit of Rs. 71,000 with the licensee within four weeks, without prejudice, the stay to stand automatically vacated on default. On 9 May 2023 none appearing to press even in revised call, the writ was dismissed for want of prosecution.

not_decided.point: Whether provisional and final assessments were served and whether the Electricity Act, 2003 and U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005 were complied with before the 9 May 2011 citation, and the merits of the theft assessment
not_decided.note: 2011 Bench found the matter required consideration after counsel could not state the mode of sending the assessments; 2023 dismissal decided nothing on those issues
